title: Manchester United and Lammens: time to decide in goal
body:
Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens is under fire after two major mistakes in a 2-2 draw with Sporting [S1]. The question now is whether Mauricio Pochettino should drop him [S1].

Jamie Carragher has said Lammens' confidence is a real worry, and argued that one costly howler cost Pochettino a first win since taking charge [S2]. Sky Sports frames it differently, suggesting the manager will feel his side were robbed of a better result [S2]. Both takes point at the same problem: the goalkeeper is the one carrying the blame.

The wider form makes the debate harder to wave away. In their last five league matches, United have won none, drawn two and lost three, collecting just two points [ST1]. They have scored five and conceded 14 in that spell, a sequence of DLLDL [ST1]. Numbers like those do not hide behind one bad afternoon, and a leaking defence makes every goalkeeping wobble look louder.

Patience has a shelf life, and this is where it starts running out. A rough patch becomes a habit very quickly between the posts, and the coach needs a settled answer rather than another week of guesswork.

The Touchline Take: confidence is the hardest thing to rebuild in goal, so the decision needs making before the next mistake makes it for them.
